# Google Workspace SAML Federation — facts

> Source-anchored units about Google Workspace SAML Federation: 16 across 4 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · 16 units · 4 sources · rights: quote -->

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Configure a custom SAML app in Google Admin. Exchange Google SSO URL, Entity ID and signing certificate for Atlas ACS URL and Audience URI; Atlas supplies the Start/Login URL. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation · also: https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/set-up-your-own-custom-saml-app
- [statement] Enable the SAML app for everyone or selected organizational units/access groups, and test the login flow. App assignment is a separate setup step from creating the SAML metadata. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation · also: https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/set-up-your-own-custom-saml-app
- [statement] Enable Signed Response for the Atlas custom app. Google otherwise signs only the assertion by default, while the MongoDB setup explicitly requires a signed response. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation · also: https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/set-up-your-own-custom-saml-app

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Google documents a maximum of 75 groups in a custom SAML app group-membership mapping. This is a Google app configuration limit, not evidence of an Atlas-wide group limit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/set-up-your-own-custom-saml-app · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] StrongDM describes its G Suite SSO–MongoDB Atlas connection as a custom StrongDM integration for unified access. Its page is evidence for an intermediary access product, rather than instructions for configuring native Atlas SAML federation. (low confidence) — https://www.strongdm.com/connect/g-suite-sso-mongodb-atlas · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Google Workspace can act as the SAML identity provider for Atlas UI access, letting assigned users sign in with corporate credentials; this configuration does not itself establish database authentication. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/operator/current/ak8so-configure-federated-authentication.md
- [statement] MongoDB specifies HTTP POST request binding, SHA-256 response signature algorithm, Signed Response enabled, Name ID format UNSPECIFIED and Primary Email as Name ID for the Workspace integration. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation
- [statement] Map Google first and last name fields to case-sensitive firstName and lastName. A Workspace user reported that missing these mappings caused new-user SSO failures at okta/hooks/acserror even while existing users could log in. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/mongodb-atlas-okta-integration-login-error/230897
- [statement] Optional Atlas role mapping uses a single Google group-membership mapping row containing all selected groups and the app attribute memberOf. Google includes only the selected groups to which the user belongs, directly or indirectly. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation · also: https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/set-up-your-own-custom-saml-app
- [statement] Verify and associate an email domain in Atlas to route matching sign-ins to Google Workspace. If multiple SAML identity providers share that domain, MongoDB says the cloud console routes to the first configured one; use a specific SP- or IdP-initiated URL for an alternative. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation
- [statement] Before testing domain routing, MongoDB recommends saving the Bypass SAML Mode URL, retaining the Federation Management Console session, and testing in a private browser window. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation
- [statement] MongoDB documents Google Workspace as a SAML identity provider for signing in to Atlas and other MongoDB cloud services; Google supports custom SAML applications using managed Google Account credentials. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation · also: https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/set-up-your-own-custom-saml-app
- [statement] MongoDB specifies HTTP POST binding and SHA-256, Name ID format UNSPECIFIED with Primary Email, and case-sensitive firstName and lastName attribute mappings. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation
- [statement] Users need the Google SAML application enabled for them. Google supports enabling access for everyone, organizational units or access groups; its guide also requires matching sign-in email addresses. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation · also: https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/set-up-your-own-custom-saml-app
- [statement] Apono advertises Google Workspace-driven granular permissions and access-request workflows as capabilities of connecting Apono with Google Workspace. That page does not establish equivalent native Atlas SAML database-permission automation. (low confidence) — https://www.apono.io/wiki/connecting-idps-with-databases/google-workspace/connect-google-workspace-with-mongo-atlas/ · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation
- [statement] Google requires a super administrator for the documented custom SAML app setup. MongoDB separately requires Atlas Organization Owner access and describes the Google prerequisite more broadly as administrative privileges. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-google-ws.md · keywords: Google Workspace SAML Federation · also: https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/set-up-your-own-custom-saml-app
